questions.question_english: A female contractual sanitation worker (sweeper) outsourced to a school reports to the Principal that the school's Head Clerk demanded sexual favours in exchange for approving her monthly attendance sheet. Under the POSH Act, 2013, what is the appropriate institutional mechanism to handle this complaint?
options_english: She must approach the Local Complaints Committee (LCC) directly because contractual staff cannot access an Internal Committee
The school's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) has full jurisdiction to receive and inquire into the complaint
The Principal must personally conduct a private inquiry and summarily dismiss the Head Clerk
The complaint can solely and exclusively be adjudicated by the regional Labour Court
questions.explanation_english:
Under Section 2(a) and Section 2(f) of the POSH Act, 2013, the scope of statutory protection is comprehensive:
1. 'Aggrieved woman' under Section 2(a) means a woman of any age, whether employed or not, who alleges having been subjected to any act of sexual harassment in a workplace.
2. 'Employee' under Section 2(f) explicitly includes a person employed for any work on regular, temporary, ad hoc, daily wage, or contractual basis, either directly or through an agent/contractor, with or without the knowledge of the principal employer.
Because the alleged harassment occurred within the school premises (the workplace) and was perpetrated by an employee of the establishment (the Head Clerk), the school's Internal Complaints Committee (ICC) has undisputed statutory jurisdiction to inquire into the matter. The Principal cannot bypass the ICC to conduct a private inquiry, nor does the contractual nature of the worker require routing the matter to the Local Committee (LCC), which is reserved for units without an ICC or where the respondent is the employer himself.
questions.explanation_hindi:
पॉश अधिनियम, 2013 की धारा 2(a) और 2(f) के तहत कानूनी संरक्षण का दायरा अत्यंत व्यापक है:
1. धारा 2(a) के अनुसार, 'व्यथित महिला' (Aggrieved Woman) का अर्थ किसी भी आयु की ऐसी महिला से है, चाहे वह उस संस्थान में नियोजित हो या नहीं, जो कार्यस्थल पर लैंगिक उत्पीड़न की शिकार हुई हो।
2. धारा 2(f) के अंतर्गत 'कर्मचारी' की परिभाषा में नियमित, अस्थायी, संविदात्मक (contractual), दैनिक वेतनभोगी, या ठेकेदार के माध्यम से आउटसोर्स किए गए सभी कर्मी शामिल हैं।
चूँकि घटना विद्यालय परिसर (कार्यस्थल) में हुई है और आरोपी प्रधान लिपिक विद्यालय का कर्मचारी है, इसलिए विद्यालय की आंतरिक शिकायत समिति (ICC) को इस शिकायत को स्वीकार कर विधिवत जांच करने का पूर्ण वैधानिक अधिकार प्राप्त है। प्रधानाचार्य को स्वयं व्यक्तिगत जांच करने का अधिकार नहीं है, और न ही संविदा कर्मचारी होने के आधार पर पीड़िता को LCC जाने की बाध्यता है (LCC केवल तब आवश्यक होती है जब संस्थान में ICC न हो या आरोपी स्वयं नियोक्ता हो)। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: Which Constitutional Amendment Act paved the way for the introduction and implementation of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime in India?
options_english: 101st Constitutional Amendment Act
100th Constitutional Amendment Act

questions.explanation_english:
The Goods and Services Tax (GST) was introduced in India through the Constitution (One Hundred and First Amendment) Act, 2016, which received Presidential assent on September 8, 2016 and came into full legal effect on July 1, 2017.
Key constitutional provisions introduced by this amendment include:
- Article 246A: Conferred concurrent powers on Parliament and State Legislatures to make laws with respect to goods and services tax.
- Article 269A: Provided for the levy and collection of GST on inter-state supply and imports by the Government of India, to be apportioned between the Union and the States.
- Article 279A: Established the Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council) chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
(Note: The 100th Amendment dealt with the Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh; the 73rd introduced Panchayati Raj in 1992; and the 105th restored state governments' power to identify Socially and Educationally Backward Classes).

भारत में वस्तु एवं सेवा कर (GST) को 'संविधान (एक सौ एकवाँ संशोधन) अधिनियम, 2016' के माध्यम से लागू किया गया, जिसे 8 सितंबर 2016 को राष्ट्रपति की स्वीकृति प्राप्त हुई तथा 1 जुलाई 2017 से राष्ट्रव्यापी रूप से प्रभावी किया गया।

- अनुच्छेद 246A: संसद और राज्य विधानसभाओं को वस्तु एवं सेवा कर लगाने हेतु समवर्ती विधायी शक्तियां प्रदान की गईं।
- अनुच्छेद 269A: अंतर-राज्यीय आपूर्ति और आयात पर केंद्र सरकार द्वारा जीएसटी लगाने व वसूलने तथा उसे केंद्र और राज्यों के बीच विभाजित करने का प्रावधान किया गया।
- अनुच्छेद 279A: जीएसटी परिषद (GST Council) के गठन का प्रावधान किया गया, जिसकी अध्यक्षता केंद्रीय वित्त मंत्री करते हैं।

questions.explanation_english:
Section 35 of the POCSO Act, 2012 establishes specific statutory timelines to ensure the speedy trial of sexual offences against children:

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding Article 15(5) of the Constitution of India:
I. It applies to admission to both aided and unaided private educational institutions.
II. It applies to minority educational institutions referred to in Article 30(1).
III. It empowers the State to make reservations for socially and educationally backward classes.
IV. It applies only to higher education and not to school education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and III only
I, II and III only
III and IV only
I, III and IV only
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I and III are correct, whereas statements II and IV are incorrect.
- Statement I is correct: The text of Article 15(5) explicitly encompasses 'private educational institutions, whether aided or unaided by the State'.
- Statement II is incorrect: Article 15(5) contains an express exclusionary proviso: 'other than the minority educational institutions referred to in clause (1) of article 30'. Minority institutions are completely exempt from the purview of Article 15(5).
- Statement III is correct: The clause empowers the State to enact provisions for the advancement of any socially and educationally backward classes (SEBCs) or for the SCs and STs relating to admissions.
- Statement IV is incorrect: Article 15(5) applies to 'educational institutions' generally without any restriction to higher education. It applies to primary, secondary, and higher secondary schools as well. In fact, Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act (25% quota in private schools) draws constitutional legitimacy from Article 15(5).
Therefore, only statements I and III are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I और III सही हैं, जबकि कथन II और IV गलत हैं।
- कथन I सही है: अनुच्छेद 15(5) के मूल पाठ में स्पष्ट रूप से लिखा है कि यह प्रावधान 'प्राइवेट शिक्षा संस्थाओं में भी, चाहे वे राज्य द्वारा सहायता प्राप्त हों या सहायता न प्राप्त हों', लागू होता है।

questions.question_english: Which of the following perquisites provided by an employer to a government school employee is completely exempt from income tax (tax-free perquisite)?
options_english: Laptop or computer provided for official and personal use
Government-provided rent-free unfurnished residential accommodation
Interest-free personal loan of ₹1,00,000 provided by the employer
Services of a domestic sweeper/servant paid for by the employer
questions.explanation_english:
Under Rule 3(7)(vii) of the Income-tax Rules, 1962, the provision of a computer or laptop (including hardware and accessories) by an employer to an employee or any member of their household for official and/or personal use is classified as a completely tax-free perquisite with a taxable perquisite value of NIL.
In contrast, other facilities attract taxable perquisite valuation under Rule 3:
- Rent-free accommodation (Rule 3(1)): For government employees, the perquisite value is taxable based on the license fee determined in accordance with government rules.
- Interest-free loans (Rule 3(7)(i)): Loans exceeding ₹20,000 provided interest-free or at concessional rates create a taxable perquisite based on the SBI lending rate.
- Sweeper/domestic servant (Rule 3(3)): The actual wages paid or reimbursed by the employer constitute a taxable perquisite.
Therefore, only the laptop/computer is a 100% tax-free perquisite.

1. नियोक्ता द्वारा कर्मचारी या उसके परिवार के सदस्यों को आधिकारिक अथवा व्यक्तिगत उपयोग के लिए कंप्यूटर या लैपटॉप प्रदान करना पूर्णतः कर-मुक्त अनुलाभ (Tax-free Perquisite) माना जाता है (इसका करयोग्य मूल्य शून्य होता है)।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the institutional safety protocols and POCSO guidelines recommended for schools:
I. Every school must establish an internal Child Abuse Monitoring Committee (CAMC) / Child Safety Committee.
II. Teachers and staff members should be trained not to ask probing, suggestive, or leading questions if a child discloses sexual abuse.
III. To safeguard the school's reputation and avoid panic among parents, the administration may resolve the matter internally without reporting it to the police.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
Statements I and II are correct, while Statement III is completely false and unlawful:
- Statement I is correct: Under NCPCR and CBSE POCSO safety guidelines, schools are mandated to establish a Child Abuse Monitoring Committee (CAMC) or Child Safety Committee to maintain vigilance, oversee child safety, and manage grievance mechanisms.
- Statement II is correct: Staff members must be trained to receive disclosures with empathy and calmness, strictly avoiding interrogative, judgmental, or leading questions that could traumatize the child or distort factual recall.
- Statement III is incorrect: Under Section 19 and Section 21 of the POCSO Act, 2012, reporting any knowledge or apprehension of child sexual abuse to the police/SJPU is mandatory. Concealing an offence or failing to report it under the pretext of protecting institutional reputation or handling it internally is a criminal offence punishable under Section 21 with imprisonment of up to six months or one year (for in-charge/heads) or fine or both.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I और II सही हैं, जबकि कथन III पूर्णतः गलत और गैर-कानूनी है:
- कथन I सही है: NCPCR तथा CBSE के पॉक्सो दिशा-निर्देशों के अनुसार, प्रत्येक विद्यालय में बाल सुरक्षा की निगरानी एवं शिकायतों के निवारण हेतु 'बाल उत्पीड़न निगरानी समिति' (CAMC) अथवा बाल संरक्षण समिति का गठन किया जाना अनिवार्य है।
- कथन II सही है: शिक्षकों एवं कर्मचारियों को संवेदनशील बनाया जाना आवश्यक है ताकि वे प्रकटीकरण (disclosure) के समय बच्चे से अनावश्यक, दबाव डालने वाले या भ्रामक प्रश्न (leading questions) न पूछें, जिससे बच्चे पर मानसिक दबाव न पड़े और साक्ष्य प्रभावित न हों।
- कथन III गलत है: पॉक्सो अधिनियम की धारा 19 के तहत मामले की सूचना पुलिस/SJPU को देना अनिवार्य वैधानिक दायित्व है। संस्था की प्रतिष्ठा बचाने के नाम पर रिपोर्ट न करना धारा 21 के तहत एक संज्ञेय अपराध है, जिसके लिए संस्था प्रमुख को कारावास व जुर्माने का दंड हो सकता है। अतः केवल कथन I और II सही हैं। इसलिए विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (a) I and II only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Schools must form child abuse monitoring committees and train staff to avoid asking probing or leading questions when receiving disclosures. Concealing incidents or withholding reports from police to protect institutional reputation violates Section 19 and Section 21, attracting severe criminal penalties for institutional leadership under statutory provisions.

Consider the following components of receipts/income that may pertain to a school Principal or their family:
I. Dearness Allowance

questions.explanation_english: Under Section 17(1) of the Income Tax Act, 1961, payments made by an employer to an employee during or arising out of service—such as Dearness Allowance (DA), Transport Allowance, and House Rent Allowance (HRA)—are classified and taxed under the head 'Income from Salaries'. In contrast, 'Family Pension' received by the surviving spouse or legal heir of a deceased employee is paid after the employee's death. Because there is no employer-employee relationship between the government and the surviving legal heir, family pension is assessable under the head 'Income from Other Sources' under Section 56(2)(ia), subject to standard deduction under Section 57(iia). Therefore, only items I, II, and IV are taxed under Salaries.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 17(1) के अंतर्गत नियोक्ता द्वारा कार्यरत कर्मचारी को प्रदान किए जाने वाले भत्ते जैसे महंगाई भत्ता (DA), परिवहन भत्ता (Transport Allowance) और मकान किराया भत्ता (HRA) 'वेतन से आय' शीर्ष के अधीन कर-योग्य होते हैं। इसके विपरीत, कर्मचारी के निधन के उपरांत उसके विधिक वारिस/आश्रित पति या पत्नी द्वारा प्राप्त 'पारिवारिक पेंशन' पर कोई नियोक्ता-कर्मचारी संबंध लागू नहीं होता, इसलिए इसे धारा 56 के तहत 'अन्य स्रोतों से आय' शीर्ष में रखा जाता है (जिसमें धारा 57(iia) के तहत मानक कटौती मिलती है)। अतः केवल I, II और IV ही 'वेतन' शीर्ष के अंतर्गत आते हैं।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following sequence of events regarding a Drawing and Disbursing Officer's (DDO) responsibilities and an employee's rights:
I. An employee fails or refuses to submit Form 12BB and investment proofs within the timeline set by the school.
II. The DDO calculates TDS under Section 192 without granting unverified deductions and deducts tax accordingly.
III. The employee later files their personal Income Tax Return (ITR) with the Income Tax Department and claims deductions based on actual eligible investments, seeking a refund.
Is the above sequence legally valid and acceptable under Income Tax rules?
options_english: No, the DDO commits an offense by deducting excess tax without considering eligible deductions.
No, employees are legally barred from claiming deductions in their ITR if omitted from employer declarations.
Yes, the DDO is legally protected and the employee can claim eligible deductions and refund in their personal ITR.
Yes, but the DDO must report the unverified investment claims in Part B of Form 16.
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 192 read with Rule 26C of the Income Tax Rules, 1962, a DDO is legally prohibited from allowing tax deductions without having received Form 12BB along with substantiated documentary proof. If an employee fails to submit proofs within the stipulated deadline, the DDO is legally bound to compute TDS on the basis of available records without allowing unverified deductions. This procedure protects the DDO from penalties for short deduction under Section 201. Simultaneously, the employee does not forfeit their statutory rights; under Section 139 and Section 237, the employee can claim all bona fide Chapter VI-A deductions while filing their personal ITR and receive a refund of excess TDS deducted directly from the Income Tax Department.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम की धारा 192 और नियम 26C के तहत DDO केवल उन्हीं कटौतियों को स्वीकार कर सकता है जिनके लिए कर्मचारी ने फॉर्म 12BB और दस्तावेजी साक्ष्य प्रस्तुत किए हों। साक्ष्य न मिलने पर DDO बिना कटौती के TDS काटने के लिए विधिक रूप से बाध्य है और धारा 201 के तहत किसी भी शास्ति से सुरक्षित रहता है। वहीं दूसरी ओर, कर्मचारी के वैधानिक अधिकार समाप्त नहीं होते हैं; धारा 139 के तहत अपना व्यक्तिगत आयकर रिटर्न (ITR) भरते समय वह अपने सभी वैध निवेशों का दावा कर सकता है तथा धारा 237 के तहत अधिक कटे हुए कर का रिफंड सीधे आयकर विभाग से प्राप्त कर सकता है। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।

key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Yes, DDO is covered and employee can claim refund in ITR.

questions.question_english: In a situation where the Drawing and Disbursing Officer (DDO) has deducted TDS from an employee's salary but fails to deposit it into the Central Government account, what statutory protection is available to the employee under the Income Tax Act, 1961?
options_english: The employee is legally required to pay the tax amount once again directly to the Income Tax Department
Section 205 legally bars the income tax authorities from demanding payment of tax directly from the employee where tax has already been deducted
The employee receives total statutory immunity from filing income tax returns for the subsequent five financial years

questions.explanation_english: Section 205 of the Income Tax Act, 1961 provides express statutory protection to taxpayers from whom tax has already been withheld at source. It states that where tax is deductible at source, the assessee (employee) shall not be called upon to pay the tax himself to the extent to which tax has actually been deducted from that income. The CBDT, through Office Memorandums and instructions (e.g., Instruction No. 275/29/2014-IT(B)), as well as several landmark High Court judgments, has reiterated that the tax recovery proceedings for deducted but unremitted TDS can only be instituted against the defaulting deductor/employer as an 'assessee-in-default' under Section 201, and cannot be recovered from the employee whose tax was deducted at source.
questions.explanation_hindi: आयकर अधिनियम, 1961 की धारा 205 करदाता (कर्मचारी) को स्पष्ट सांविधिक संरक्षण प्रदान करती है। धारा 205 के अनुसार, जहां किसी आय से स्रोत पर कर की कटौती कर ली गई है, उस सीमा तक संबंधित करदाता से दोबारा कर भुगतान की मांग नहीं की जा सकती। सीबीडीटी (CBDT) के निर्देशों (जैसे अनुदेश सं. 275/29/2014-IT(B)) और विभिन्न उच्च न्यायालयों के न्यायिक निर्णयों में यह स्पष्ट किया गया है कि यदि नियोक्ता/DDO ने वेतन से कर काट लिया है और उसे सरकारी खजाने में जमा नहीं किया है, तो आयकर विभाग कर्मचारी से उस कर की वसूली नहीं कर सकता। विभाग धारा 201 के अंतर्गत दोषी कटौतीकर्ता (DDO) को ही 'डिफ़ॉल्ट में निर्धारिती' मानते हुए ब्याज और जुर्माने सहित वसूली की कार्यवाही करने के लिए बाध्य है। अतः विकल्प B सही उत्तर है।

questions.question_english: Every Government establishment is required to maintain records of the persons with disabilities employed by them under the RPwD Act, 2016. Who among the following is statutorily authorized to inspect these records?
options_english: Any citizen of India applying under the Provisions of RTI Act without any conditional restrictions
Only the respective Head of the Department or the designated Appointing Authority
The Chief or State Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities
Members of the National Human Rights Commission acting exclusively under statutory powers
questions.explanation_english: Under Section 22 of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, every government establishment is mandated to maintain records regarding persons with disabilities employed, facilities provided, and other particulars, which must be open to inspection. Sections 75(1)(h) and 80(c) empower the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities (at the Union level) and the State Commissioners (at the State/UT level) to monitor the implementation of the Act, look into complaints, and inspect records maintained by establishments. Under the Act, Commissioners have the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, including the power to requisition and inspect public records to enforce compliance with reservation rosters and workplace accessibility norms.

questions.question_english: Does the legal obligation to report under Section 19 of the POCSO Act require absolute proof of the commission of an offence?
options_english: Yes, an FIR can only be filed with concrete physical or forensic evidence
No, mere apprehension or knowledge triggers the duty to report
Yes, direct eyewitness testimony is mandatory before reporting to police
No, but the Principal's personal satisfaction is required before reporting
questions.explanation_english: Section 19(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012 clearly specifies that 'apprehension that an offence under this Act is likely to be committed or knowledge that such an offence has been committed' is sufficient to trigger the statutory obligation to report. Absolute proof, forensic evidence, or eyewitness testimony is not required. The law intentionally sets the threshold at 'apprehension' or 'knowledge' so that child protection agencies and law enforcement can intervene promptly to protect the victim and collect evidence, rather than leaving the burden of verification on school teachers or administrators.
questions.explanation_hindi: पॉक्सो अधिनियम, 2012 की धारा 19(1) में स्पष्ट रूप से उल्लेख है कि यदि किसी व्यक्ति को 'यह आशंका हो कि इस अधिनियम के तहत कोई अपराध किया जाना संभावित है या यह ज्ञान हो कि ऐसा अपराध किया गया है', तो उसे तत्काल रिपोर्ट करना होगा। इसके लिए किसी पूर्ण या प्रत्यक्ष फॉरेंसिक साक्ष्य अथवा चश्मदीद गवाह की आवश्यकता नहीं होती। कानून का उद्देश्य यह सुनिश्चित करना है कि संदेह उत्पन्न होते ही जांच एजेंसियां और बाल संरक्षण इकाइयां सक्रिय होकर बच्चे की सुरक्षा कर सकें, न कि स्कूल प्रशासन सबूत जुटाने में समय बर्बाद करे।

questions.explanation_english:
Form 16 consists of two distinct parts:

1. Part A: It is a standardized, digitally signed document downloaded directly by the employer from the TRACES (TDS Reconciliation Analysis and Correction Enabling System) portal of the Income Tax Department. It contains:
   - Name, address, PAN, and TAN of the employer/deductor.
   - Name, address, and PAN of the employee.
   - Summary of quarterly tax deducted (from Form 24Q filings) and actual date and challan identification details (BSR code, challan serial number) of tax deposited into the Central Government account.

2. Part B: Prepared by the employer (annexed to Part A), detailing gross salary, exempt allowances under Section 10 (e.g. HRA, conveyance), standard deduction under Section 16(ia), deductions under Chapter VI-A (80C, 80D, etc.), net taxable income, and final tax computation.

key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) SC, ST, OBC, or a group disadvantaged by social, economic, or gender factors.

Section 2(d) defines a child belonging to a disadvantaged group to include children belonging to Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, socially and educationally backward classes, or categories facing disadvantages due to gender, disability, or socio-cultural barriers hindering educational participation.
